newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates dip amid dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates dip amid dull trade.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates dipped amid dull trade on Saturday on lack of buying interest by mill owners on the first day of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, dealers said.
"Attendence was thin and trading dull because it was the first day of Ramadan," dealer Kishan Chand said. "Bank were also closed."

He said the mill owners were short of cash and only going for good quality stocks which were not much in evidence. "We expect a rise in cotton rates as this year's crop has been much less than earlier estimates."
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 variety was traded at 2,150 rupees ($53.45) per maund (37.32 kg), dealers said.
